extracted.intended_audience: comedy writers and social-media video creators (Twitter/YouTube)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating short-form comedy bits and viral videos that use disproportionate production value and committed execution to amplify a single absurd idea; includes advice on platform fit, recurring annual bits, and knowing when to retire a bit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the disproportion between effort and silliness maximal?
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the production effort is wildly out of proportion to the silliness of the idea; the disproportion itself functions as the joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A joke video gets funnier as production gets more inappropriate. Example: a musical number with one absurd lyric is funny; a musical number with full choreography, costume changes, and orchestration for ONE absurd lyric is much funnier. The disproportion between effort and silliness IS the joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is there ONE single silly idea, executed completely?
rubrics_metrics.description: Pick one singular, silly idea and execute it with absolute commitment and completeness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single-idea maximalism: choose ONE silly idea and use technical excellence and disproportionate resources to commit fully. The joke is often the commitment to that single idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the platform suit the joke (text vs. video vs. live)?
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure the medium (Twitter, video, live performance) matches what the joke requires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twitter rewards SPEED of joke; video rewards COMMITMENT of joke. Don't confuse the two — if a Twitter joke demanded a video, it probably wasn't strong enough. Choose the platform that amplifies the joke's necessary element (speed vs. commitment).

rubrics_metrics.name: If recurring, is each iteration meaningfully escalated?
rubrics_metrics.description: For recurring/annual bits, each new iteration should both escalate production and offer a different angle to maintain interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An annual bit builds expectation; each iteration must escalate the production AND vary the angle. Part of the audience's laughter comes from the fact that you're still doing it, so escalation and variation are essential to keep it fresh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are you committing more than the audience expects you to?
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether your level of commitment and production exceeds audience expectations in a way that produces humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committing more than the audience expects is a core lever for funniness — it creates surprise and highlights the disproportion. However, monitor for diminishing returns: if the audience stops being surprised, the effect fades.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do you know when to retire it?
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize when a bit has run its course and should be ended rather than repeated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A bit is over when the audience has stopped being surprised by the commitment. One good annual bit beats five mediocre ones. Know when to stop and retire the bit to preserve its impact.
